calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Rangers
calls.body: The Rangers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Capitals’ kill is near the bottom of the league. The Capitals need to stay out of the box.
calls.call: The Rangers’ power play creates at least their usual 8.3 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: NY Rangers 5th for power play (8.3 expected goals per 60) · Washington 27th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: NY Rangers’s power play created 9.7 expected goals per 60 in 4:53 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 8.3, and scored 1 goal.

calls.head: The Rangers feed on mistakes, and the Capitals make them
calls.body: The Rangers turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Capitals are the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Capitals.
calls.call: The Rangers get at least their usual 7.6% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: NY Rangers 10th for chances off turnovers (7.6% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Washington 32nd for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 5 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: 17.6% of NY Rangers’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.6%.

WSH.head: We had this close to even (49% for Washington), and Washington came through.

NYR.head: We had this close to even (51% for NY Rangers), and it went Washington’s way.

surprises.head: A big night for L. Thompson
surprises.body: L. Thompson allowed 1 goal on shots worth 2.9 expected goals, 1.9 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 9 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: The Capitals beat the Rangers
paras: Alexis Lafrenière opened the scoring midway through the first. Boone Jenner scored the winner late in the second.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way.

items.text: The Rangers’ four-game winning streak is over.
Marcus Pettersson faces his old team, Vancouver, on Sunday.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
